harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Joined node1's two segments (eth1↔node2, eth2↔node3) into one L2 domain via a Linux bridge (br0, STP off, no IP) on node1, assigned node2/node3 eth1 into a shared 192.168.50.0/24 subnet, verified direct ping and correct MAC learning per port (transparent bridging, not routing). Config persisted via a systemd oneshot unit on node1 (SONiC/Debian) and /etc/network/interfaces on node2/node3 (Alpine). Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes with boot_id-based proof of restart and post-restart recovery verification.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 interfaces and routes to map topology: node1 eth1<->node2 eth1, node1 eth2<->node3 eth1, both segments previously unaddressed L2-only links
On node1 (SONiC-VS/Debian): neutralized docker0 class-E leakage, stopped interfaces-config.service/networking.service, flushed eth1/eth2, created br0 bridge with STP disabled, enslaved eth1+eth2

Assigned node2 eth1 = 192.168.50.11/24 and node3 eth1 = 192.168.50.12/24, verified direct ping across the bridge with correct FDB MAC learning per port and no IP on br0 (proving forwarding not routing)
Persisted the bridge setup via a new systemd oneshot service (antrieb-l2-bridge.service) on node1, enabled at boot after sonic.target/interfaces-config.service
Persisted eth1 static addressing via /etc/network/interfaces on node2 and node3 (Alpine/OpenRC)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, bridge state, container health, working pings) on all three nodes

Restarted node1, node2, then node3 sequentially (never concurrently), polling until exec access returned, confirming boot_id changed each time, and re-verifying bridge/service/connectivity recovery after each restart before moving to the next node
Final post-all-restarts check confirming br0 still has no IP and FDB shows node2's and node3's MACs learned on the correct respective ports

evidence.requirement: Baseline: original segmented topology (node1 eth1/eth2 unaddressed, node2/node3 eth1 down)
evidence.summary: Showed node1's eth1/eth2 as separate link-local-only interfaces, node2/node3 eth1 down, confirming two distinct segments prior to bridging

evidence.requirement: SONiC pre-config cleanup (docker0 de-neutralized, reconcilers stopped) before bridging
evidence.summary: Removed docker0's class-E IP and stopped interfaces-config/networking services on node1 per SONiC reference guidance

evidence.requirement: Single L2 domain created with node1 forwarding (bridge), not routing
evidence.summary: br0 created enslaving eth1+eth2 in forwarding state; node2/node3 addressed into shared 192.168.50.0/24; successful ping node2->node3 across the bridge; FDB shows per-port MAC learning; br0 carries no IP, confirming L2 forwarding not L3 routing
Installed and enabled antrieb-l2-bridge.service on node1 (recreates bridge at boot); added static eth1 stanzas to /etc/network/interfaces on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline on all nodes
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, bridge forwarding state, SONiC container health on node1, and working cross-segment pings from node2/node3 before any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; boot_id changed from 1f515f97... to 030ffac9...; post-restart bridge auto-recreated via systemd unit, all SONiC containers active, cross-node ping succeeded

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 208921d8... to 7f2c37ac...; eth1 static IP persisted and ping to node3 succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 384aa966... to 02f40386...; eth1 static IP persisted and ping to node2 succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: Final verification: L2 domain and bridging behavior intact after all three sequential restarts
evidence.summary: FDB shows node2's and node3's MACs learned on the correct respective bridge ports (eth1/eth2); br0 has no IP address, confirming node1 forwards frames transparently rather than routing
